newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Britain wants debt write-offs for poorest - minister.
newsitem.headline: Britain wants debt write-offs for poorest - minister.

text.p: Britain would like to see foreign debt written off in the world's poorest countries, according to British Parliamentary Under Secretary for International Development George Foulkes.
Foulkes told reporters on Tuesday that debt relief should however be tied to democracy and good governance in these countries.

He said the new British government strongly supported debt relief and was pushing the issue among the Paris Club, the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and other multinational lending institutions.
"We wrote off the debt of Botswana in the 1960s," he said, referring to the former British colony. "It was a good start and a good example."

Britain's overall development programme totalled 2.2 billion pounds ($3.6 billion), 40 percent of which went to European Union projects. A further 50 percent was used in bilateral development aid, while the remaining 10 percent was other multilateral aid.
